THE JOURNEY, IN ORDER

1 Landing        ← here
2 Sign up        ← here
3 Welcome
4 Your goal
5 Build profile
6 Questions
7 Applications (empty)
8 New application
9 Tailoring
10 Review
11 Applications (full)
12 Profile

Screens land on this canvas as we work through them.

WHY THIS HEADLINE

"You'll apply to forty jobs. You'll tailor maybe five." names the behaviour rather than pitching the product — the reader recognises themselves before they have been sold anything. Italic serif carries the turn in the sentence.

STRUCTURE

Numbered sections (01–04) give the page a spine, so it reads as an argument rather than a stack of blocks.

The product shot sits directly under the hero and bleeds off the bottom edge — the page shows the tool before it describes it.

Two dark bands (the numbers, the closing call) break up a long light page and give it rhythm. The close inverts the button so the last thing on screen is the loudest.

The stats are real and sourced. Cost carries a [YOUR PRICE] placeholder — fill it before launch rather than letting a made-up number ship.

One field, or one button. Nothing is asked here that the flow asks better later — no name, no role, no password if they use Google.

The line about deleting your data sits above the fold on purpose: this is the screen where someone decides whether to hand over their work history.
